faq.a: Click Add to Server at the top of this page (or /invite), pick your server, and authorize. You need Manage Server permission in that server. Then run /setup in the server and open the dashboard to configure it.
faq.q: How do I add the bot to my server?

faq.a: Every slash-command reply is ephemeral by design — only you can see it, so command spam never clutters the channel. The only public posts are the ones a command is meant to make in a channel: poll embeds, announcements, suggestions, FAQ replies, starboard posts, and trade proposals.
faq.q: Why are all command replies only visible to me?

faq.a: An admin runs /ticket-setup in the channel for the ticket panel. Members click the button to open a ticket; staff use /ticket-claim, /ticket-add, /ticket-remove, and /ticket-close. Category, log channel, and support role live on the dashboard Tickets tab.
faq.q: How do I set up tickets?

faq.a: An admin runs /application-create (name, description, up to 5 questions) then /application-open. Members apply with /apply; staff review with /application-list, /application-view, /application-accept, and /application-deny. See the Applications guide above.
faq.q: How do I set up applications?

faq.a: An admin runs /stream-add for a Twitch or YouTube streamer (or adds them on the dashboard Streams tab) and picks an announcement channel. The bot posts when they go live. Use /stream-template to rename a channel while someone is live — see the Streams guide above.
faq.q: How do I set up streams?

faq.a: Leveling runs automatically: members earn XP from chatting and commands. Check progress with /rank, see the top 10 with /leaderboard, and set levels with /setlevel (admin). Level-up messages and level roles are on the dashboard Leveling tab.
faq.q: How do I set up leveling?

faq.a: Invite tracking is automatic once the bot has Manage Server permission — it compares its cached invite list to the live list on every join to find the inviter. See stats with /invites and /inviteleaderboard, details with /invite-info, and reset with /invite-reset (admin). The fake-account age threshold is on the dashboard Invites tab.
faq.q: How do I set up invites?

faq.a: In MySQL, per-server: every row carries a guild_id, so no server can see or affect another server's data. That covers settings, tickets, applications, economy balances and inventories, starboard posts, message logs, polls, and bot-tracking flags.

The bot backs up the whole database every day at 3 AM (configurable) and keeps the last 30 days. The owner can run one on demand with /backup, and staff can see backup files and the run log on the Staff → Backups page. Restore with: node scripts/restore-db.js <file> --confirm.

Every error and warning the bot hits is written to the MySQL error_logs table and to logs/bot-errors.log on the host. Staff can browse them on the Staff → Errors page or with /errors, and read one in full with /error <id>.
faq.q: How do I report an error / where do errors go?

faq.a: Run /stream-template set with a template that contains {name} (you can also use {game} and {title}), max 100 characters — or set it on the dashboard Streams tab, which shows a live preview. The channel renames when a streamer goes live and restores its original name when they go offline.
faq.q: How do I change the live-channel name template?

faq.a: On the host: git pull (and npm install if package.json changed), then npm run deploy to re-register the slash commands, then restart the bot (npm start, or your process manager). The current version and what changed are on the /version page.
faq.q: How do I update the bot?

gettingStarted.intro: Four steps and the bot is running in your server.

steps.body: Click the Add to Server button (top of this page, or /invite). Pick your server and authorize. You need Manage Server permission in that server. The bot asks for the permissions it needs to do its jobs (read/send messages, manage roles for auto-role and shop roles, manage channels for tickets and server stats).
steps.title: 1. Add the bot to your server

steps.body: If you host the bot yourself, the dashboard starts in setup-wizard mode on first run: open the one-time setup link it prints to the console (or in setup-token.txt) and walk through 8 steps — bot token, client ID, database, dashboard, API keys, backups. The wizard tests the bot token and the database connection before saving, and writes config.json for you. No manual file editing needed.
steps.title: 2. Run the first-run setup wizard

steps.body: Discord (required): https://discord.com/developers/applications — bot token + client ID. Twitch (stream alerts): https://dev.twitch.tv/console. YouTube (stream alerts + music search): https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/library/youtube.googleapis.com. Steam (profile lookups): https://steamcommunity.com/dev/apikey. Everything else works without a key.
steps.title: 3. Get API keys (only the ones you need)

steps.body: Run /setup in your server (sets the welcome channel, log channel, and ticket settings), then open the dashboard, pick your server, and work through the tabs — General, Moderation, Tickets, Streams, Leveling, and the rest. Every setting saves to the database and applies within a minute, no restart needed.
steps.title: 4. Configure your server

gettingStarted.title: Getting started

steps: An admin runs /ticket-setup in the channel where the ticket panel should live.
Members click the panel button to open a private ticket channel.
Support staff use /ticket-claim to take it, /ticket-add and /ticket-remove to manage who can see it, and /ticket-close to close it (a transcript is saved).
Ticket category, log channel, and support role are set on the dashboard Tickets tab (or with /setup).
guides.title: Tickets

steps: An admin runs /application-create with a name, a description, and up to 5 questions, then /application-open to accept applications.
Members apply with /apply and answer the questions in a modal.
Staff review with /application-list (pending counts), /application-view to read one, and /application-accept or /application-deny — accepting can grant a role and DMs the applicant.
Check your own applications anytime with /application-status. Manage forms on the dashboard Applications tab.
guides.title: Applications

steps: An admin runs /stream-add (Twitch or YouTube) and picks the announcement channel, or adds streamers on the dashboard Streams tab.
When a streamer goes live, the bot posts an announcement embed. /stream-announce posts one manually (handy for Facebook/TikTok).
To rename a channel while someone is live: /stream-template set with a template containing {name} (also {game} and {title}), max 100 characters — or set it on the Streams tab with the live preview.

The channel is renamed only on live/offline transitions, and restores its exact original name when the stream ends. Discord allows about 2 renames per 10 minutes per channel, so the bot queues retries instead of failing.
guides.title: Streams + live channel name

steps: An admin runs /welcome-setup with a channel and a message template — placeholders: {user}, {username}, {server}, {membercount}.
Turn them on/off with /welcome-toggle, and preview one with /welcome-test.
Goodbye messages work the same way: /goodbye-setup and /goodbye-toggle.
Both can also be configured on the dashboard Welcome tab, with a live preview as you type.
guides.title: Welcome messages

steps: An admin runs /automod-setup: spam limits (messages per window), what happens on spam (delete / warn / timeout), link and invite blocking, and the log channel.
Add banned words with /automod-words add, remove with /automod-words remove, list with /automod-words list.
Exempt roles or channels with /automod-exempt so staff and announcement channels are never filtered.
View current settings anytime with /automod. Everything is also on the dashboard Automod tab.
guides.title: Automod

steps: An admin runs /suggestions-setup with the channel suggestions go to.
Members submit with /suggest (title + details in a modal). The bot posts it with 👍 / 👎 voting — one vote per user.
Staff review with /suggest-status (your own) or the dashboard Suggestions tab, and Approve, Deny, or mark Implemented.
The suggester is told the outcome.
guides.title: Suggestions

steps: Everyone starts with 100 coins. Earn more with /daily (once a day, 100–500 coins plus a random daily item) and /work (once an hour, 50–250 coins).
Check your wallet and bank with /balance, move coins with /deposit and /withdraw, send coins with /pay, and see the richest members with /eco-leaderboard.
Spend in the shop: /shop lists items, /buy <id> buys (role items grant the role, everything else lands in /inventory). One item per guild per day is 25% off as the daily deal.

Crates (Common 500, Rare 1,500, Legendary 5,000) are opened with /open-crate for random loot. Sell items back with /sell (usually half price). Trade with another member using /trade — they accept, you confirm, and the swap happens in one database transaction.
Feeling lucky? /slots, /blackjack, /roulette, /gamble-coinflip, and /gamble-dice all use the same wallet. Minimum bet 10, maximum 10,000, 5 seconds between games.
guides.title: Economy, crates & trading

steps: An admin runs /starboard-setup with a channel and a threshold (default 3 stars).
When a message collects that many ⭐ reactions, the bot posts it to the starboard channel as an embed (author, content, jump link, star count, first image).
The count updates live as stars arrive. If it drops below the threshold, the starboard post is deleted.
Bot messages and messages already in the starboard channel are ignored.
guides.title: Starboard
